 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Tennis fans criticized Roger Federer for missing Stan Wawrinka's farewell ceremony at the Swiss Indoors in Basel, questioning the Swiss legend's absence during a significant moment for his compatriot.
 Wawrinka played the final ATP match of his 24-year professional career on Tuesday, suffering a first-round defeat to eighth-seeded Jiri Lehecka at his home tournament. The three-time Grand Slam champion lost 7-5, 7-6(7-2), with his final shot being a one-handed backhand that landed just wide.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Ahead of the match, the tournament held an hour-long farewell ceremony on center court, featuring video tributes, music, and heartfelt messages from Wawrinka's parents. However, Federer's absence drew attention from fans on X, with several questioning why the 20-time Grand Slam champion did not attend the event. One fan criticized Federer for missing the occasion, writing:
 "Federer not showing up for Wawrinka's final match was an insult. The ATP sportsman of the year for a decade should have attended the event and showed his respect in person."
 Another user described the absence as both sad and strange, pointing out Federer's connection to Basel.
 "Very strange and sad tbh, Federer was born in Basel and still only lives a couple of hours away from it."
 Mocking Federer for not attending the farewell, another follower commented:
 Along similar lines, a few other fans chimed in:
 Meanwhile, Novak Djokovic approached Swiss Indoors tournament director Roger Brennwald to ask whether he could be present on court for Wawrinka's farewell ceremony on Monday night, according to Swiss newspaper Blick .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Stan Wawrinka opened up about his farewell at the Swiss Indoors
 During the post-match press conference of the Swiss Indoors on Tuesday, Stan Wawrinka reflected on his farewell and said he was pleased to end his career while still feeling competitive, as per atptour.com .
 "I have always dreamed of being able to finish feeling good, being competitive, and that's what I was able to do. This year has been amazing with a great amount of emotion, a lot of sadness at every tournament where you say goodbye. But it has been much more beautiful than I could have ever dreamed, than I could have imagined," said Wawrinka.
 He added:
 "I have received so much love, I have lived through so many emotions in my last year at 41, feeling competitive. I have played top players, I have played young players as well. I have had very good matches. For me, it's an ideal ending."
 Wawrinka also expressed appreciation for the support he received from fans and the tournament, saying the farewell was beyond what he could have imagined years earlier.
